newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Markets see Portugal in EMU - finance minister.
newsitem.headline: Markets see Portugal in EMU - finance minister.

text.p: The convergence of Portugal's long-term rates with those of major European economies shows markets already view the country as making the grade for Economic and Monetary Union (EMU), Finance Minister Antonio Sousa Franco said.
"At this moment, we are practically in the Euro as far as the financial markets are concerned," he told Reuters, referring to the name of the European Union's planned single currency.
Sousa Franco was attending the swearing-in of officials of Portugal's newly-formed Institute of Public Debt.

The spread between Portugal's 10-year state bond and the German equivalent has narrowed to around 125 basis points from over 450 basis points a year ago as confidence has mounted that Portugal will be in the vanguard of countries to launch EMU in 1999. --Sergio Goncalves, Lisbon bureau 3511-3150035
